sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real-Time Video Matching and Cross-Border Social Telephony

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties (e.g., with Hong Kong, South Korea, Kuwait, Mexico)
EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (applicable via EU membership)
EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (applicable via EU membership)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law), incorporating EU Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 January 2019 implementing the UBO register; Law of 25 March 2020 amending the AML/CFT Law; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; and applicable CSSF circulars on AML/CFT and sanctions screening.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Extract from commercial register of each corporate partner (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry of the corporate partner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for the person executing the incorporation deed on behalf of any partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the partner's country of residence or formation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Good standing certificate (attestation de l'impôt / attestation de non-faillite) of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax, court or registry authority in the partner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in UBO's jurisdiction of residence or passport issuing authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs, general partners and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC's SDN List, CSSF/PSF blacklists, and PEP databases per FATF Recommendations 12 and 22. Enhanced due diligence applies for high-risk payment rails (Apple IAP/Paymentwall) and cross-border personal data flows. Ongoing transaction monitoring and PEP status risk scoring are required for the SCSp's beneficial owners and business counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal: www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be written in Latin characters. If a non-Latin script is used, a certified transliteration into Luxembourgish, French, German or English must be filed. The name must be distinctive and not misleading. For an SCSp, the name must contain the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the suffix 'SCSp' (or 's.c.sp.'). Luxembourgish, French, German and English are accepted by the RCS; other languages are permitted if the name can be transliterated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the name by the LBR or by the notary during incorporation, the applicant may request a written statement of grounds within 15 days. An administrative reconsideration may be filed with the LBR. If the registry maintains the refusal, the applicant may bring summary proceedings (référé) before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, Commercial Chamber, within one month of notification; the court may order registration if the rejection is deemed unlawful. Legal counsel should be engaged to comply with the procedural deadlines and grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A mere virtual office is not sufficient for an active video-chat and cross-border social telephony business. Luxembourg law requires a real registered office (siège social) in the Grand Duchy. Administrative domiciliation can be used only if the SCSp has genuine substance (physical premises, personnel, business records) in Luxembourg; for a data-centric app with cross-border payment rails, the authorities expect a verifiable local presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high for this activity; estimated 35% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg tax administration (AED) or the CSSF, increasing to 50% if the payment rails include high-risk PSPs or if the SCSp is used for intercompany fund flows.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) name clearance and preliminary search fee
Notarial fee for draft and execution of incorporation deed for SCSp (including articles of association)
Registration of the incorporation deed in the Luxembourg Recueil électronique des sociétés and RCS filing (registration inscription)
UBO declaration filing with the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (first submission)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legalization/apostille and sworn translation of foreign corporate partners' and UBOs' identity and corporate documents
AML/CFT and PEP/sanctions compliance screening setup (UBO and partner risk file, transaction monitoring framework for payment rails)
Registered office (domiciliation) pre-incorporation commitment fee (to secure physical address until opening of bank account)
Legal opinion and corporate due diligence memorandum for pre-incorporation (covering RCS name clearance, SCSp law, VAT/AML aspects)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Company Law), notably Articles 1, 14, 15, 16 and 907-1 to 907-10 (SCSp regime); and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg register of commerce and companies (RCSL), as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCSL), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (Acte de Constitution) filed via the RCSL e-filing platform and published in the Luxembourg Official Gazette (Mémorial C, Recueil des Sociétés et Associations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital; SCSp may be established with zero paid-up capital, and capital contributions are freely determined by the partnership agreement; since the SCSp does not have legal personality, capital is held by the general partner (gérant) for account of the partnership and may be paid in cash or in kind; any escrow/blocked account requirement applies only if the partnership agreement or a regulated activity so requires. For a non-regulated video-matching app, no statutory escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF THE SCSP. The general partner, acting as management body, resolves: (1) to subscribe and admit the initial limited partner for the committed contribution described in the partnership agreement; (2) to adopt as the SCSp's registered office the address set out in the deed of constitution; (3) to appoint the designated manager (gérant) with sole authority to represent the SCSp and to open bank accounts; (4) to approve the execution and filing of the incorporation deed with the RCSL and the publication in the Mémorial; and (5) to authorize the manager to procure all operational licenses and registrations for the video-matching application. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the SCSp corporate name and verify availability at the RCSL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCSL) – online name reservation portal via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the RCSL e-filing portal or via a certified local professional (notaire/avocat). Provide the proposed corporate name, indicate the legal form "Société en Commandite Spéciale" or "SCSp", and confirm that the name does not contravene Luxembourg public order or misleading-name rules. The RCSL checks identity against existing registered names, protected names, and trademarks. The reservation is valid for a limited period; proceed promptly to notarial or authenticated deed drafting.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name reservation form
Identification documents of the general partner and initial limited partner
Brief statement of the corporate purpose (ISIC 6311 video-matching application)
Power of attorney if a local representative files the reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged, file an administrative objection with the RCSL within 15 days or submit a revised name reservation request; where refusal is based on third-party rights, obtain a written consent/waiver or select a new distinctive name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the partnership deed and articles of association before a notary or in authenticated private form
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Notaire) or a Luxembourg lawyer authorized to draft the authenticated deed; RCSL receives the filing after execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary or counsel to prepare the deed of constitution (acte de constitution) and the partnership agreement (contrat de société). The SCSp is formed by one general partner (with unlimited liability) and one or more limited partners. The deed must state the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (data processing and real-time video-matching application services), duration if not indefinite, manager/gérant appointment, contribution terms, and profit-sharing rules. The deed is executed before the notary where notarization is chosen, or in authenticated private form if the RCSL filing is made by a professional; for SCSp, private deed filing is permitted if accompanied by statutory declarations. Ensure the general partner is a Luxembourg or foreign entity with legal capacity to act.
required_dossiers: Partnership deed and articles of association in French, German, or English (with Luxembourg French version preferred)
Notarized or authenticated signatures of all founding partners
Proof of address and identity of the general partner (KYC/AML pack)
Bank confirmation of contribution account if capital is paid in cash
Power of attorney / notarized mandate for the local incorporating agent
Draft management declaration of acceptance by the appointed gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or RCSL queries the deed (e.g., defective purpose clause or missing statement), amend the deed by a supplementary notarial act and re-file within the statutory cure period; the RCSL will issue a formal notice specifying the defect, and the applicant may correct and resubmit within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation deed with the RCSL for registration and legal effectiveness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCSL) – e-filing platform (LBR eFile/Guichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized or authenticated deed, together with the completed RCSL registration form, the statement of the general partner accepting its unlimited liability, and the declaration of the manager accepting appointment. The filing is made by the notary or a registered professional on the electronic platform. Pay the applicable registration fee. The RCSL verifies completeness, registers the SCSp in the commercial register, and allocates a Luxembourg business registration number (matricule). The SCSp becomes validly constituted upon registration, unless the deed provides for later effectiveness for third parties.
required_dossiers: Original notarized/authenticated deed of constitution
RCSL standard registration form (Formulaire de dépôt électronique)
Statement of general partner acceptance of unlimited liability
Statement of appointed manager acceptance of office
Proof of payment of registration fee
Copy of tax identification number or EU TIN for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL issues a query or rejection, review the formal notice, cure the cited inconsistency by submitting supplementary declarations or an amended deed, and refile within the indicated deadline; if the refusal persists, appeal to the Luxembourg district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) in commercial matters within 15 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the statutory notice in the Official Gazette (Mémorial C)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Official Gazette (Journal Officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg – Mémorial C)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCSL registration, the registrar transmits the core legal particulars for publication in the Mémorial C. The SCSp must verify that the published notice contains the correct name, registered office, purpose, duration, manager(s), and partners. The publication is a condition for opposability of the deed vis-à-vis third parties. Where the notary files electronically, the notarial office handles publication; if filing was made privately, coordinate directly with the RCSL for the Mémorial transmission.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration confirmation
Extract of the deed prepared by the notary/RCSL
Payment confirmation of publication fee
Company details summary sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Mémorial notice contains errors, request a corrigendum from the RCSL/notary and arrange for a corrected republication; delay does not invalidate incorporation but affects third-party reliance, so promptly file a corrective addendum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Luxembourg corporate tax, VAT, and social security and obtain the business identification number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes – ACD), VAT Administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA), and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCSL registration, file the registration form with the Luxembourg direct tax administration for corporate income tax and net wealth tax purposes; register for VAT if taxable turnover is anticipated; and register the general partner (as employing entity if staff are engaged) with the CCSS. The RCSL matricule is used as the national business identifier; the ACD issues the Luxembourg tax number (numéro de registre national). The SCSp is transparent for income tax purposes, so partners are liable in their own capacity, but the SCSp must file annual declarations as required by Luxembourg tax procedure.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration certificate (extraits)
Partnership deed and articles
Name, address, and tax residence information of each partner and manager
Contact information of the appointed tax filer (fiduciary/accountant)
Declaration for VAT registration (Formulaire 10) and CCSS registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or VAT office queries classification or missing partner data, provide supplementary KYC documentation and revised forms; request a written ruling under Luxembourg advance tax ruling procedures if the pass-through characterization or permanent establishment risk is questioned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Luxembourg business bank account and deposit any agreed initial contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the general partner (e.g., Luxembourg-domiciled bank or EU branch); CSSF-regulated environment subject to AML/KYC rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCSL registration extract, partnership deed, beneficial ownership declaration, and authentic identification of the general partner and manager to the selected bank. Complete the banking KYC/AML checklist, including source of funds and anticipated transaction volumes for the video-matching application, noting the planned payment rails (Apple IAP and Paymentwall). If the partnership agreement requires a contribution to be paid in cash, arrange the transfer from the limited partner's account to the SCSp account held by the general partner; the general partner holds the funds for the account of the SCSp since the SCSp lacks separate legal personality.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration extract (recent)
Partnership deed and articles (certified copy)
Beneficial ownership register declaration (RBE extract or filing confirmation)
AML/KYC questionnaires and source of funds documentation
Identity documents of general partner, limited partner, and authorized signatories
Pro-forma invoices or business plan for the video-matching app
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays because of beneficial ownership complexity or enhanced due diligence, provide a detailed organizational chart and legal opinion from Luxembourg counsel on the SCSp structure; alternatively, approach a second EU-based credit institution or a licensed payment/e-money institution for a segregated operational account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the beneficial ownership declaration and maintain the SCSp statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE), under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCSL registration, submit the RBE filing identifying the natural person(s) who ultimately own or control the SCSp, applying the partnership control criteria. Because the SCSp has no separate legal personality, the beneficial owners are the general partner and any limited partner exercising substantial control. Maintain registers of partners, minutes of meetings, and decisions of the general partner at the registered office. Update the RBE within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership.
required_dossiers: RBE filing form with beneficial owner particulars
Ownership and control chart of the SCSp
Identity documents of ultimate natural persons
Partnership agreement excerpts evidencing profit/share rights
RCSL extract confirming registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE office rejects or queries the filing, respond to the deficiency notice by submitting the explanatory ownership documentation and corrected RBE forms; fines for late filing can be avoided by documenting the submission date and curing within the statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate for Industry and Innovation, together with the Luxembourg Regulatory Institute (Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation – ILR) for any electronic communications aspects and the Luxembourg data protection authority (Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données – CNPD) for data processing aspects
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business license/operating authorization under the amended law of 2 September 2011 on the access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist, and certain liberal professions (Loi du 2 septembre 2011) — for an online services/video-matching platform, an industrial/commercial business license (autorisation d'établissement) is generally required, supplemented by a CNPD processing authorization/registration and, where applicable, an ILR authorization for electronic communications services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Luxembourg Administration of Environment (Administration de l'environnement), under the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: The video-matching application is primarily a digital data processing service; no physical industrial installation is operated in Luxembourg, so the activity falls under Category 'Registration/No formal EIA' (not a listed Annex I/II project under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment) unless the company establishes its own data centers, cooling plants, or server facilities, which would then trigger either a 'Class 1' or 'Class 2' environmental permit evaluation in accordance with the amended Law of 8 June 1999 on classified installations (établissements classés).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any auxiliary IT/telecom infrastructure: wastewater discharge must comply with Luxembourg general wastewater standards (e.g., < 2,000 mg/L COD BOD thresholds per applicable communal discharge regulation); volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from backup generators must meet EU Industrial Emissions Directive thresholds (Directive 2010/75/EU); electronic waste handling must comply with the EU WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU) and Luxembourg national waste regulations; server heat-rejection systems must respect noise limits and energy-efficiency obligations under the EU Energy Efficiency Directive framework.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The SCSp's registered office must obtain a fire safety compliance certificate from the local communal fire brigade or the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) if premises are open to employees; structural load inspection by a certified engineering bureau if occupying dedicated office or server spaces; workplace safety clearance requires an ITM approval of workstations, electrical installation verification, and a health and safety plan in accordance with the Luxembourg Labor Code (Code du travail) and the Law of 17 June 1994 on occupational safety and health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration; Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) for entity registration; central administrative portal: myguichet.lu / guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-established foreign entity: (1) determine whether supplies qualify for the Non-Union or Union One Stop Shop (OSS) scheme, which may eliminate the need for full Luxembourg VAT registration for cross-border B2C digital services; (2) if full registration is required, file the VAT registration application with the AEDT via myguichet.lu, obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits, and appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative if the entity is established outside the EU and no reciprocal assistance arrangement applies; (3) if an SCSp is established in Luxembourg, first file the constitutive document with the RCS and obtain the national business number (matricule d'identification), then open the VAT account using that matricule; (4) provide evidence of economic activity in Luxembourg, director/manager identification, and anti-money-laundering documentation (KYC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. A Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg direct tax purposes: the entity itself is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax, and profits and losses are taxed directly at the level of its partners. For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is a taxable person in its own right when it carries on an economic activity independently, and registration thresholds apply according to normal VAT rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box classification regime. The SCSp is a contractually based special limited partnership that is transparent by default for direct tax; no direct-tax election to make the SCSp itself taxable is generally available. For VAT, the entity may elect between the normal local VAT registration route and the OSS schemes for distance sales and electronically supplied services. Luxembourg also applies the EU small-business exemption election for established taxable persons with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000, and hybrid-mismatch rules consistent with ATAD require partners/investors to align the tax classification of the SCSp with the corresponding treatment in their residence jurisdictions where otherwise a mismatch would arise.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No mandatory VAT registration threshold for non-established foreign suppliers supplying digital B2C services or goods to Luxembourg consumers; such supplies may alternatively be declared through the OSS. Luxembourg-established small taxable persons carrying on solely exempt-vulnerable activities are exempt from VAT if annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000, excluding VAT, and can opt for the normal VAT scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a real-time fiscal pre-clearance, digital stamping, or API clearance regime for generic B2B invoices. Structured e-invoicing is permitted and encouraged, and B2G suppliers to Luxembourg public entities must issue electronic invoices using PEPPOL-compliant formats. VAT returns, recapitulative statements and OSS filings are submitted electronically through the AEDT/myguichet.lu portal. Taxable persons are required to preserve all source documents, invoices and technical records for at least 10 years. Future EU ViDA reforms may introduce harmonized e-invoicing and digital reporting in later phases, but no domestic real-time clearance mandate is currently in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a 0% VAT rate applies only where goods are physically removed from Luxembourg and from the European Union to a third territory, provided the supplier obtains and maintains evidence of export, including a customs export declaration accepted by the customs authority and proof that the goods left the EU within the legally required period. Services, including video-chat and social telephony app services rendered by an SCSp, are not 'exports' in the customs sense; B2B supplies to non-EU customers are outside Luxembourg VAT via the place-of-supply rule, and B2C electronically supplied services are taxable in the customer's country, to be declared using the OSS, not zero-rated under the export provisions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Transport and Logistics Proof of Exit (e.g. CMR, airway bill, terminal discharge certificate)
Proof of Payment and FX Repatriation Records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and cross-border service claims are subject to strict AEDT documentary audit. Where the exporter or supplier cannot substantiate the physical export, the place of supply outside Luxembourg, or the reality of the cross-border transaction, the AEDT may retroactively assess VAT at the standard rate, apply monthly late interest of 0.8% on the assessed amount, and impose administrative fines that may reach 100% of the tax evaded. In cases of fraudulent export schemes, fabricated customs documentation, or abusive invoicing involving video-match and social telephony platforms, the tax authorities may extend the statute of limitations to up to 10 years, assert joint and several liability against the SCSp partners, managing directors and tax representatives, and initiate criminal tax-fraud proceedings leading to fines and terms of imprisonment under Luxembourg criminal and tax law. Under the EU anti-fraud frameworks, information exchanges via Eurofisc and mutual assistance requests increase the likelihood of cross-border clawback and enforcement in the residence jurisdiction of the beneficial operators.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — the Luxembourg member of the Eurosystem — together with the European Central Bank (ECB), which conducts monetary and foreign-exchange policy, and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which supervises credit institutions and payment institutions. Luxembourg has no separate foreign-exchange-control administration; the BCL manages foreign-exchange reserve operations delegated by the ECB and administers the balance-of-payments statistical reporting framework for resident entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls, no prior-authorisation regime, no surrender obligations and no convertibility restrictions, in accordance with Articles 63–65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Profit remittance, partnership-interest redemption, dividend and interest distributions are freely permitted without central-bank approval; the only practical hurdles are EU/Luxembourg financial sanctions, BCL external-statistics reporting thresholds, and the enhanced due-diligence documentation that Luxembourg banks require for a medium-risk online social-entertainment business such as a random video-match application.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg and the Eurozone do not impose any statutory timeline, mandatory repatriation window or forced conversion ratio for export receipts. Cross-border revenue settled by Apple and Paymentwall may be retained in EUR or converted into foreign currency freely in the market, subject only to sanctions screening and the BCL external-statistics reporting duties fulfilled through the resident banking intermediary.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. An EEA-licensed e-money institution or payment institution authorised under PSD2/EMD2 and passportable across the EU single market can onboard the SCSp remotely and can serve as a cost-efficient collection and payout rail for Paymentwall and Apple settlement proceeds; however, such institutions are not direct members of TARGET2/STEP2 clearing, commonly impose transaction-volume caps, and do not provide the full treasury function (surplus-liquidity investment, FX credit lines, wholesale recovery). Non-EEA or offshore digital EMIs are rated Low: they constitute a serious AML/CTF blocker under Luxembourg law and CSSF supervisory expectations and must not hold operational treasury balances of the SCSp.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For this Medium-Risk-Enhanced profile, first-tier Luxembourg banks in practice require the SCSp's general partner (gérant), its authorised signatories and the ultimate beneficial owners to attend an in-person or, at minimum, a video-interview KYC meeting; fully remote opening is rarely granted to an SCSp that lacks legal personality unless it is managed by a regulated Luxembourg alternative investment fund manager. The recommended onboarding path is a physical compliance meeting in Luxembourg, or a hybrid process using a Luxembourg notary's certified true-copy package together with apostilled corporate documents, passports of the UBOs and the general partner's mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is a contractual special limited partnership without legal personality, creating uncertainty about the counterparty, its legal capacity and the identity of parties legally bound by the banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full partnership agreement (contrat de société) governed by the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 which introduced the SCSp; constitutive documents filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); current extract from the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); resolution or mandate of the general partner appointing the authorised signatories; specimen signatures; and, where required by the bank, a legal-short-form opinion confirming the SCSp's capacity, representation rules and liability allocation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume micro-transactions processed through Apple IAP and Paymentwall in the online social-entertainment sector, raising money-laundering, chargeback, fraud and consumer-protection risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written business-description memorandum and revenue-flow diagram; executed merchant or developer agreements with Apple and Paymentwall; monthly reconciliation evidence linking app-store sales reports to bank and processor settlement statements; the company AML/CTF manual with automated transaction-monitoring thresholds and suspicious-transaction reporting procedures to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers); chargeback and refund policy; and geo-IP restriction and sanctions-screening rules applicable to end-users.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border proceeds originate from end-users in third countries, including potentially restricted, sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A customer-country matrix and jurisdiction risk assessment; real-time sanctions screening against EU, UN and Luxembourg consolidated lists; an end-user identity verification procedure consistent with the GDPR; contractual app-store terms and technical geo-blocking that exclude embargoed or high-risk territories; and a monitoring programme capable of reporting suspicious flows to the CRF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth for the initial capital injection and ongoing operational funding is not self-evident for a tax-transparent partnership owned by non-residents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor bank statements and tax-residency certificates; capital-call and subscription notices issued by the general partner; declarations of source of wealth covering the origin of contributed assets; UBO and politically-exposed-person questionnaires; audited or management-prepared 12-month working-capital budget; and supporting contracts demonstrating how Apple and Paymentwall settlements fund operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident investors inject equity or loan capital in EUR either through SEPA for EU-origin investors or through SWIFT MT103 for non-EU investors, to the SCSp's segregated euro account at its Luxembourg credit institution; the remittance-information field must state the SCSp name, the investor identifier and the purpose 'SCSp capital contribution / subscription', or a SWIFT category code such as '//INV//' where required by the remitting bank. The bank's verification file must contain the executed subscription agreement, a capital-call notice issued by the general partner, investor KYC/PEP questionnaires, bank statements as source-of-funds evidence and an updated RBE filing. The BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting for the inward foreign direct investment flow is discharged through the resident banking intermediary and the GP's annual external-statistics survey. Inward app-store settlements from Apple arriving as net service revenue are classified under the applicable balance-of-payments code for software or royalty services and are not treated as capital injections, although they must still be supported by the underlying Apple developer agreement for source-of-funds verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements for cloud infrastructure, content moderation, advertising, legal and tax advisory services are executed via SWIFT MT103 single credit transfers from the SCSp's EUR account, or via SWIFT MT101 multi-payment batch files for repetitive vendor sweeps; SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant are used for EU counterparties below the BCL de minimis reporting threshold, with TARGET2/STEP2 as the underlying clearing rail for same-day euro settlements. Confirmed commercial documentary credits under UCP 600, cleared through SWIFT MT700/MT710 messages, are available for large non-EU supplier contracts but are functionally uncommon for the video-app operating model. All outbound payments are free from foreign-exchange authorisation requirements, but are subject to sanctions screening at both the paying entity and the beneficiary bank, and must be captured in the BCL monthly external-statistics report whenever the counterparty is non-resident and the cumulative flow exceeds the applicable threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/GBP vanilla FX forwards with a non-speculative committed-expenditure basis
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies arising from Paymentwall settlement exposures, such as BRL, IDR, KRW and MXN
EUR/USD and cross-currency swaps (swap deposits) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with a Luxembourg banking counterparty
Bought (long) vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP currency options to hedge downside FX risk while preserving upside participation; writing options is outside an acceptable SCSp treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS annual accounts filing and publication (where statutory accounts are required or voluntarily published for the SCSp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end; for calendar-year accounts, filing due by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger court-ordered filing, daily fines up to EUR 1,500, administrative sanctions, and in persistent default, removal or strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership/transparent-entity information declaration to the Luxembourg tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June following the tax year, or such filing deadline as communicated via the eCAB portal and tax assessment procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, formal delinquency notice, tax assessment on available records, default interest, and possible administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO confirmation or update filing with the Luxembourg beneficial-owner register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership; an annual no-change confirmation is made by the registered agent as a corporate maintenance best practice where no change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and, for intentional violations, criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 or imprisonment sanctions under Luxembourg AML/CFT legislation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance of the SCSp's statutory corporate record and minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate registers maintained at the registered office; inspection by tax authorities and courts as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing maintenance with annual partner-endorsed review; records must be current as of each financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete statutory records may result in compliance deficiencies, regulatory scrutiny, fines, and adverse inferences in insolvency or audit proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SCSp is generally not a legal entity and is not automatically subject to a statutory audit. Compulsory audit arises if the SCSp qualifies as a regulated investment vehicle under the SIF, SICAR, or RAIF regimes, is authorized by the CSSF, or is otherwise subject to consolidated or qualifying thresholds applicable to the underlying general partner or managing entity: balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average full-time staff of 50 for two consecutive financial years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: If consolidated or statutory accounts are prepared, the SCSp applies Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and companies register and annual accounts, or IFRS as adopted by the EU when required for regulated funds or consolidation purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg law imposes a continuous UBO disclosure obligation. Any change in shareholding, partnership interests, or indirect controlling arrangements must be filed with the RBE within one month of the change. A formal annual confirmation is not a standalone statutory obligation for an SCSp, but the registered agent must annually review and affirm the recorded UBO data, and file an updated declaration whenever a change is identified. The general partner and each limited partner must retain underlying ownership evidence and provide it to the registered agent upon request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,600 - 3,500 per annum depending on the corporate service provider and registered agent structure
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 for regulated SCSp vehicles requiring CSSF-compliant audit; nil to USD 2,000 for simpler transparent vehicles relying on unaudited financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp partnership level (fiscally transparent pursuant to Article 7 of the Law of 12 July 2013 and general Luxembourg partnership law principles); resident corporate partner combined headline rate 24.94% calculated as 17% corporate income tax (IRC), 1.19% solidarity surcharge (7% of IRC) and 6.75% municipal business tax (Luxembourg City tariff; municipal rates vary by commune).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp itself is subject to no partnership-level corporate income tax, net wealth tax not applicable to transparent structure; each partner is taxed directly. Available incentives for corporate partners: (1) 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend income and capital gains where the partner holds at least 10% or a EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost for an uninterrupted 12-month period; (2) 80% IP-Box exemption on qualifying intellectual property income (patents, copyrighted software), yielding an effective cash tax rate of approximately 4.99% on qualifying video-matching software/licensing revenue; (3) 50% exemption for dividend income from small participations under Article 115bis LIR (applicable from fiscal year 2024); (4) EUR 17,500 municipal business tax allowance for qualifying commercial activities; (5) minimum net wealth tax of EUR 570 per year for eligible holding corporate partners; (6) optional opaque status election under Article 175 LIR available but rarely advisable for fund-type SCSp structures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) together with Form 500 (impôt commercial communal) and Form 600 (impôt sur la fortune); e-filed through MyGuichet.lu / eCDF electronic filing portal of the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers: statutory filing due 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end; e-filing concession routinely extends the deadline to 31 December; newly incorporated taxpayers must file within 3 months of commencement/registration (option to extend via tax advisor).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal name, RCSL (trade and companies register) number, legal form, principal activity (ISIC 6311), address of registered office and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partner filing in its own capacity must quote its Luxembourg tax file number, appoint a Luxembourg tax representative, and attach certified English or French translations of constitutional documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp transparency status: declaration that the entity is a Société en Commandite Spéciale and that no corporate income tax liability arises at partnership level; allocation schedule identifying each partner's profit/loss sharing percentage and distributable taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are taxable in Luxembourg only to the extent the SCSp carries on a Luxembourg permanent establishment or fixed base; otherwise enter 'not taxable in Luxembourg' and claim DTA protection through the PE threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after deductions, loss carry-forward, and participation exemption claims; disclose intercompany transactions and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partner with Luxembourg-source income must attach full supporting accounts; losses are allocable only against the partner's Luxembourg-source profits and expire after the 5-year carry-forward window.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of Luxembourg-sourced dividends, interest and royalties allocable to partners; declaration of withholding tax positions and DTA relief claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficiary claiming 0% or reduced treaty rate must submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate and file Luxembourg Form 210 with the payer before distribution; refund claims must be lodged within the 3-year limitation period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax; default interest accrues at 0.8% per month on unpaid tax; failure to file despite formal notice triggers an administrative compulsion penalty of EUR 1,200 to EUR 25,000 and criminal fines under Articles 96-97 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung); wilful non-filing can escalate to imprisonment of up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510/560 interposed as annual partner allocation statement for SCSp and transparent partnerships; submitted electronically via the eCDF/MyGuichet account of the General Partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 30 June following the fiscal year-end, mirroring Form 510; cooperative filers on eCDF receive automatic extension to 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of each General Partner and Limited Partner, their country of residence, share of income/loss, allocations of royalties, dividends, and capital gains generated by the video-match application.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where all partners are non-resident and no Luxembourg PE exists, the SCSp should be flagged as 'fiscally transparent, non-resident partners only' with no Luxembourg tax liability; retain TRCs in the partnership file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Foreign tax credit and withholding schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of Luxembourg WHT, if any, passed through to partners, and corresponding foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must evidence home-country taxes and availability of credit; preserve underlying tax vouchers for 10 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Omission of accurate partner allocation triggers administrative fine of EUR 500 to EUR 10,000 per infraction; the tax administration may recharacterize undistributed profits as taxable to the General Partner at the 24.94% combined rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax rate under Article 147 LIR; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate partner holds at least 10% continuously for 12 months and meets anti-hybrid conditions; 0% or reduced rates under comprehensive double tax treaties (selected treaties 5% for portfolio, 0% for qualifying substantive holdings). For SCSp, profit distributions are generally not treated as dividends because the partnership is transparent; a 15% WHT will instead attach only where the underlying payment is Luxembourg-source income allocated to a non-resident partner without treaty protection or where an Article 175 LIR opaque election is made.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state tax authority, submit it to the Luxembourg paying agent before the distribution, and file Luxembourg Form 210 (demande de réduction de la retenue à la source) through the eTax/eCDF portal; the paying agent retains a certified copy for 10 years; where WHT has been over-deducted, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes within 3 years of the withholding date; treaty shopping and lack of beneficial ownership (e.g. shell SCSp) voids relief and triggers recapture at 15% plus interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory withholding tax under Article 147 LIR; treaty-protected rates commonly 0% (e.g. US, FR, NL) or 5%; royalties for software license of the video-matching app paid to non-resident related parties require economic substance in Luxembourg. Interest: no statutory Luxembourg WHT on arm's-length corporate-to-corporate lending; 15% WHT applies from 25 February 2023 to interest paid to non-resident private individuals, to non-resident companies resident in non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, and to taxpayers not subject to corporate income tax in their residence state; treaty rates for corporate lenders typically 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory simplified transfer pricing documentation under Article 56bis LIR; EUR 5,000,000 aggregate annual controlled transactions triggers full Master File / Local File and contemporaneous benchmarking evidence under Article 56ter LIR; documentation must be prepared no later than the date of filing of the corporate income tax return and produced within 15 days of request by the tax authorities.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not codify a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute comparable to UAE onshore/DIFC regimes, but substance is enforced through: (i) beneficial ownership analysis applied by the Luxembourg tax administration and the OECD Multi-Lateral Instrument, (ii) Limitation on Benefits clauses in Luxembourg double tax treaties (e.g. Article 24 of the US-Luxembourg Treaty), (iii) European Commission State aid substance doctrine and EU ATAD anti-abuse rules, and (iv) EU Unshell/ATAD III Directive scrutiny of shell entities from 2024. For an SCSp, the General Partner must maintain demonstrable substance in Luxembourg - local registered office, local bank account, real board meetings, appropriate human resources, books and records - and must satisfy the commercial reasonableness of the video-match app value chain; a bare IP-holding SCSp with no local substance risks treaty denial, WHT recapture and reassessment at 24.94%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Luxembourg-source revenues of the video-match application, fabricating non-existent foreign expenses, or routing profits through artificially interposed shell partnerships with no economic activity for the purpose of evading the 24.94% combined corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at 24.94% plus 10% late-filing surcharge and 0.8% monthly default interest; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years under Articles 96 and 97 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law; publication of the tax decision in case of aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The General Partner (Gérant) of an SCSp is personally, jointly and severally liable for the debts and tax obligations of the partnership; a fraudulent under-declaration allows the Revenue to pierce the veil, claim civil restitution against personal assets, impose travel bans on directors pending criminal proceedings, and obtain imprisonment sentences of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SCSp with no local management, no employees, no Luxembourg bank account, no board minutes and passive ownership of the video app IP, while nonetheless claiming treaty benefits, EU directives or Luxembourg participation exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and Directive relief, retroactive 15% withholding tax on distributions, reclassification of the structure as fiscally non-transparent or void for tax purposes, penalties for non-compliance with UBO registration (EUR 110 to EUR 1,250,000), and exposure to EU Unshell Directive penalties once transposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the General Partner are jointly liable for the resulting tax shortfall and WHT; in severe cases, fraudulent misrepresentation triggers criminal liability, freezing orders over personal assets, and restriction of the right to manage companies in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party transactions (royalties, service fees, platform commissions, IP transfers) with unsubstantiated prices, missing Article 56bis/56ter files, or booking profits in low-tax jurisdictions without the required functional, capital and risk substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary tax adjustment adding back non-arm's-length payments, secondary adjustment treating the excess as a deemed dividend subject to 15% withholding tax, penalty of 25% on the additional assessment, monthly default interest of 0.8% on underpaid tax, and documentary fines for failure to produce TP files.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved transfer prices lacking an economic or functional basis face civil liability in the amount of the tax adjustment, potential wrongful trading claims by the SCSp's creditors, and criminal sanction for complicity in tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Apple IAP or Paymentwall merchant rails to process video-match transactions while obscuring the identity of beneficiaries, accepting proceeds from fraudulent chat schemes, laundering illicit funds through successive SCSp distributions, or failing to conduct customer due diligence where the SCSp is deemed to exercise a financial/commercial activity subject to the Law of 12 November 2004.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for legal entities, administrative sanctions by the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), criminal conviction for money laundering punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and confiscation of assets, and freezing of the Paymentwall/Apple merchant account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the General Partner face personal criminal conviction, travel bans, and confiscation orders; proof of knowing participation pierces the corporate veil, leading to unlimited personal liability for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Profit Distribution / Withholding Tax Misclassification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making non-arm's-length deductible payments labelled as interest, royalties, management fees or platform commissions to non-resident partners or related parties in jurisdictions that do not tax such income, in substance distributing profits of the SCSp while circumventing the 15% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of payments as dividends or quasi-dividends under Articles 164 and 168 LIR, 15% withholding tax reclaimed from the payer, denial of the expense deduction leading to tax at 24.94%, 10% surcharge, and monthly default interest during any litigated period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The General Partner's directors are jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax and interest; deliberately structuring sham payments constitutes tax evasion and attracts the same personal criminal exposure as fraudulent under-declaration.
